checks: No eclipse at 1 of 18 covered epochs where the 1.61715 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 390780000 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.6171 days. The primary eclipse causes a 3.20% dimming in the star's light, detected with a high signal-to-noise ratio of 167.8 in the automated transit search. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, though with a centroid offset of 2.4 arcsec. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find in the TESS survey data. The pipeline's machine learning model assigned it a screening score of 0.12, indicating lower confidence that this represents a genuine stellar system. The light curve data passed all quality checks without flagged issues.
